head: The matchup inside the matchup
paras: The Devils (8-5-0) lost 5-2 to Colorado on Wednesday, while the Golden Knights (9-4-1) beat Ottawa 4-1 on Tuesday. Going in, the Devils are third in the Metropolitan (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Golden Knights second in the Pacific (tied for fourth).

The Devils have played better than their record (.615) says: their chances are worth about .747, and their goaltending has held them back. The Golden Knights’ record (.679) is about what their chances are worth.

The Devils keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), throw more pucks at the net than almost anyone (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th). The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st) and block more shots than almost anyone (3rd). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), and the Devils’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. The Knights’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Devils’ not so much.

Jack Hughes (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 13 GP) leads the Devils in scoring, and Nico Hischier (7 G / 2 A / 9 P in 13 GP) has a team-high seven goals. Jack Eichel (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 14 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and Mark Stone (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Connor Hellebuyck (1-0-0 / .944 SV% in 1 GS) is expected to start for New Jersey, and Adin Hill (5-1-0 / .895 SV% in 6 GS) for Vegas.

items.text: The Golden Knights are newly without Carter Hart. Adin Hill is expected to start.
Brayden McNabb is set to play his 900th NHL game.
Jack Hughes has three goals on chances worth about 6.8 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Mitch Marner has a point in eight straight games.

VGK.head: Leaning the Golden Knights’ way
VGK.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Vegas has home-ice advantage. The Devils can still swing it if they keep the shots coming.

NJD.head: Close, but the Golden Knights have the slight edge
NJD.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Vegas has home-ice advantage. The Devils can tip it if they keep the shots coming.

calls.head: The matchup inside the matchup
calls.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Golden Knights are the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.

calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Golden Knights are near the top at keeping shots away. We’ll side with the Devils.

calls.head: Active D vs. Forward-led
calls.body: On shots from defensemen, Vegas is one of the league’s best, but New Jersey is near the bottom. Watch the Golden Knights’ defensemen jump into the play.
